newsitem.title: UK: UK major bank lending up 4.556 bln stg in November.
newsitem.headline: UK major bank lending up 4.556 bln stg in November.

text.p: The British Bankers Association said on Thursday total sterling lending by major British Banks rose a seasonally-adjusted 4.556 billion stg in November.
The rise was inflated by around 800 million stg as a result of a "substantial intragroup transaction".
"But even taking account of this, underlying lending was well up on both the October figure of 2.817 billion stg and the six monthly average of 2.953 billion stg," the BBA said.
Consumer credit rose 351 million stg , well down on the October figure of 504 million.
Tim Sweeney, director general of the BBA, said demand for credit came from a wide range of sectors.

"The major banks' lending in November was driven by demand from across the economic sectors. The rise in lending to the personal sector of 951 million stg was down somewhat on October, with the growth in consumer credit more retrained than of late," he said.
Mortgage lending rose 610 million stg compared with 623 million in October.
Lending to the financial sector rose very strongly, by 1.88 billion following a decline in October.
lending to the manufacturing sector overall fell by 84 million stg.
